chunks.title: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP)
chunks.content: Authority: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). Primary Statute: Companies Act 2017. Portal: eServices (eservices.secp.gov.pk). Regulatory Mandate: Corporate incorporation, corporate filings, single member company regulation, and director accountability.

chunks.title: Federal Board of Revenue (FBR)
chunks.content: Authority: Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). Primary Statute: Income Tax Ordinance 2001. Portal: Iris (iris.fbr.gov.pk). Regulatory Mandate: National Tax Number (NTN) registration, Active Taxpayer List (ATL) management, federal sales tax on goods, and withholding tax compliance.

chunks.title: Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB)
chunks.statute: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 154A) & PSEB Policy Guidelines
chunks.content: Authority: Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB). Primary Statute: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 154A) & PSEB Policy Guidelines. Portal: pseb.org.pk. Regulatory Mandate: Registration of IT & ITeS exporters and freelancers. Eligible registered exporters who realize export proceeds in foreign exchange through formal banking channels may avail concessionary tax treatment under Section 154A, subject to conditions and rates specified in the applicable Finance Act.

chunks.title: Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA)
chunks.statute: Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012
chunks.content: Authority: Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA). Primary Statute: Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012. Portal: pra.punjab.gov.pk. Regulatory Mandate: Levy and collection of provincial sales tax on services rendered in Punjab (standard rate 16%, with specific or reduced rates on designated IT/ITeS services as updated in provincial schedules).

chunks.title: Sindh Revenue Board (SRB)
chunks.statute: Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act 2011
chunks.content: Authority: Sindh Revenue Board (SRB). Primary Statute: Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act 2011. Portal: srb.gos.pk. Regulatory Mandate: Levy and collection of provincial sales tax on services rendered in Sindh (standard rate 13%, with reduced/concessionary rates on IT services as updated in provincial schedules).

chunks.title: Deadline: Annual Income Tax Return (Individuals & AOPs)
chunks.content: Compliance Event: Annual Income Tax Return (Individuals & AOPs). Statutory Deadline: September 30 each year (unless formally extended by FBR). Legal Consequences of Non-Compliance: Delay past statutory deadline leads to exclusion from the Active Taxpayer List (ATL) and higher withholding tax deductions (typically 100% higher under Tenth Schedule). FBR allows restoration to ATL upon filing the return and paying the applicable surcharge under Section 182A, with the ATL register updated on a daily basis.

chunks.title: Deadline: Annual Income Tax Return (Companies / Pvt Ltd)
chunks.content: Compliance Event: Annual Income Tax Return (Companies / Pvt Ltd). Statutory Deadline: December 31 each year (for tax year ending June 30, unless extended). Legal Consequences of Non-Compliance: Statutory default penalties under Section 182, exclusion from ATL, and potential loss of tax concessions until return is filed and applicable surcharge is paid.

chunks.title: Deadline: Withholding Tax Statements (Section 165)
chunks.content: Compliance Event: Withholding Tax Statements (Section 165). Statutory Deadline: As prescribed by FBR rules / applicable Finance Act (e.g. quarterly, biannual, or monthly depending on taxpayer category; verify current Iris schedule). Legal Consequences of Non-Compliance: Penalties under Section 182 for non-filing or late submission of withholding statements under Section 165.

chunks.title: Deadline: Mandatory Record Retention
chunks.content: Compliance Event: Mandatory Record Retention. Statutory Deadline: Minimum 6 years from the end of the relevant tax year (Section 174(3)). Legal Consequences of Non-Compliance: Under Section 174, failure to maintain and produce accounts/records upon notice may trigger default penalties under Section 182, best-judgment assessment by the Commissioner under Section 121, and potential disallowance of unsubstantiated business expense claims during audit.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Vague termination rights or notice periods
chunks.content: Risk Category: Vague termination rights or notice periods. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: Contracts using phrases like 'reasonable notice' without defining exact calendar days (e.g., mutually agreed benchmarks such as 30, 60, or 90 days in writing), creating commercial ambiguity and leaving eviction or exit deadlines vulnerable to dispute under contract law.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Unclear payment terms or late-payment consequences
chunks.content: Risk Category: Unclear payment terms or late-payment consequences. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: Agreements lacking defined payment milestones, bank details, grace periods, or containing vague penalty threats like 'landlord/client may take appropriate action' rather than specified liquidated terms.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Unilateral price/fee changes
chunks.content: Risk Category: Unilateral price/fee changes. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: Clauses permitting one party to unilaterally increase prices, fees, or charges without requiring bilateral written agreement or signed change-orders.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Auto-renewal without clear notice requirements
chunks.content: Risk Category: Auto-renewal without clear notice requirements. Severity: Medium Risk. Legal Details: Locking the business into an automatic renewal term unless canceled within a narrow, easily missed notice window, frequently combined with an uncapped rent or rate escalation.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Unclear ownership of intellectual property
chunks.content: Risk Category: Unclear ownership of intellectual property. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: Client pays for custom software or creative deliverables but only receives a limited license or 'right to use', while the vendor retains all underlying copyright and source code ownership.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Broad or unclear liability/indemnity clauses
chunks.content: Risk Category: Broad or unclear liability/indemnity clauses. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: One-sided commercial clauses forcing the small business to indemnify the other party for unlimited losses, or capping the counterparty's liability to an ambiguous or negligible amount.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Confidentiality and business-data handling not clearly defined
chunks.content: Risk Category: Confidentiality and business-data handling not clearly defined. Severity: Medium Risk. Legal Details: Failing to define agreed commercial safeguards regarding the permitted use, protection, return, or secure deletion of proprietary client data, credentials, and customer records upon contract termination.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Unclear subcontracting/third-party access
chunks.content: Risk Category: Unclear subcontracting/third-party access. Severity: Medium Risk. Legal Details: Allowing a contractor or vendor to delegate core performance obligations to third-party subcontractors without prior written notice or client approval, diluting confidentiality.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Missing scope, deliverables or acceptance criteria
chunks.content: Risk Category: Missing scope, deliverables or acceptance criteria. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: Agreements leaving project scope and specifications to be 'discussed later as business needs arise', guaranteeing scope creep, delivery disputes, and uncompensated revisions.

chunks.title: Contract Trap: Tax/withholding responsibilities not clearly specified
chunks.content: Risk Category: Tax/withholding responsibilities not clearly specified. Severity: High Risk. Legal Details: Failing to clarify whether agreed amounts are inclusive or exclusive of applicable withholding taxes (such as Section 153 for supplies/services or Section 155 for rent, where the payer is a prescribed withholding agent) and provincial sales tax, risking unexpected payment deductions.

chunks.title: What should I check before signing a commercial lease?
chunks.statute: Provincial Rented Premises Legislation / Contract Act 1872 / Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 155)
chunks.content: Question: What should I check before signing a commercial lease?. Legal Guidance: Verify 6 critical commercial areas: (1) Clear written termination notice (mutually agree on a realistic benchmark such as 60-90 days, rather than vague 'reasonable notice'), (2) Clear division of maintenance obligations (landlord structural vs tenant internal operations), (3) Agreed renewal terms and rent escalation mechanisms (commonly negotiated around 8-10% annually), (4) Explicit security deposit refund timeline, (5) Commercial zoning compliance under local development authority, and (6) Withholding tax treatment under Section 155 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (if the tenant is a prescribed withholding agent). Note that statutory rent rules vary by province (e.g. Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009, Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance 2001, Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance 1979).. Governing Legal Basis: Provincial Rented Premises Legislation / Contract Act 1872 / Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 155)

chunks.title: Can I terminate this contract early, and what notice is required?
chunks.content: Question: Can I terminate this contract early, and what notice is required?. Legal Guidance: Early termination rights depend strictly on the express terms of the contract and the nature of any default. Avoid vague phrases like 'reasonable notice' and define exact written timelines. Where a party commits a default, agreements commonly provide a 14 to 30-day 'Notice to Cure' before termination, though whether a cure period applies depends on the contract terms and whether the breach is fundamental under Sections 39 and 73 of the Contract Act 1872. Always review early exit penalties and security deposit forfeiture terms.. Governing Legal Basis: Contract Act 1872 (Sections 39, 73, 75) & Specific Relief Act 1877

chunks.title: Who is responsible for taxes or withholding on this payment?
chunks.statute: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Sections 152, 153, 155, Tenth Schedule) & Provincial Sales Tax on Services Acts
chunks.content: Question: Who is responsible for taxes or withholding on this payment?. Legal Guidance: Every entity is responsible for its own net income tax liability. However, where a payer qualifies as a 'prescribed person' (which includes corporate companies, registered partnerships/AOPs, and individuals whose turnover exceeds statutory thresholds under Section 153), they are legally obligated to deduct advance withholding tax at source before making payment. Withholding rates on goods, services, and contracts vary depending on the transaction type, recipient classification, and Active Taxpayer List (ATL) status under the First and Tenth Schedules of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. Contracts must explicitly state whether prices are 'inclusive' or 'exclusive' of applicable withholding and provincial sales taxes.. Governing Legal Basis: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Sections 152, 153, 155, Tenth Schedule) & Provincial Sales Tax on Services Acts

chunks.title: What records should my business maintain for tax purposes?
chunks.statute: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 174) & Income Tax Rules 2002 (Rule 29)
chunks.content: Question: What records should my business maintain for tax purposes?. Legal Guidance: Under Section 174 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 and Rule 29 of the Income Tax Rules 2002, businesses must maintain complete books of accounts, including serially numbered sales invoices, purchase bills, payment vouchers, bank account statements, and salary withholding records. These records must be retained for a minimum of 6 years from the end of the relevant tax year to substantiate deductions during audit or assessment.. Governing Legal Basis: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 174) & Income Tax Rules 2002 (Rule 29)

chunks.title: What registrations or compliance steps apply to my business?
chunks.statute: FBR Iris Guidelines / SECP Companies Act 2017 / Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 154A) / PSEB Policy
chunks.content: Question: What registrations or compliance steps apply to my business?. Legal Guidance: Business compliance follows a 4-tier structure: (1) Federal Tax registration on FBR Iris for an NTN, (2) Entity legal formation (Sole Proprietorship, Form C with Registrar of Firms for AOPs, or SECP incorporation for companies under Companies Act 2017), (3) Provincial Sales Tax on Services registration (PRA in Punjab, SRB in Sindh, KPRA in KPK) if rendering services, and (4) Sectoral registration (such as PSEB for IT exporters seeking concessionary tax treatment under Section 154A, subject to export remittance realization and current Finance Act conditions).. Governing Legal Basis: FBR Iris Guidelines / SECP Companies Act 2017 / Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 154A) / PSEB Policy
